evidence.section: 4. Tensile and low-cycle fatigue test results
evidence.quote: The study of Appa Rao et al. [11] showed similar tendencies on HIPed alloy 718 and inferred the gradual decrease in ductility of the alloy at elevated temperature was due to the persistence prior particle boundaries (PPBs) decorated with highly stable and brittle oxides and MC carbides.

evidence.section: 4. Tensile and low-cycle fatigue test results
evidence.quote: Some researchers explained that twins form as the results of annealing following plastic deformation [11,17] and the presence of twins in the HIPed alloy is found to be a desirable microstructural feature for improvement of mechanical properties.

evidence.section: 4. Tensile and low-cycle fatigue test results
evidence.quote: Bricknell [15] showed that elevated temperature tensile behavior of rapidly solidified and HIP processed Rene 80 alloy gave the lowest ductility values in the temperature range of 800–1000 °C and has been attributed to the grain boundary embrittlement.

evidence.section: 4. Tensile and low-cycle fatigue test results
evidence.quote: Prakash et al. [16] have suggested that the ductility of a superalloy Nimonic APK 1 HIPed at different temperatures gradually decreased with increasing temperature and attains a lowest value at 760 °C due to the embrittlement associated with the environmental oxidation affecting adversely the inter-particle bonding.
